summary: Christopher Minkowski is an Indologist who studied at Harvard College, the University of Delhi, and Harvard University under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He held posts at Cornell University and served as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Oxford.

Christopher Morris worked in history, archaeology, and Tibetology. He taught English literature as a professor at Keio University and lectured at the University of Tokyo and Tokyo University of Literature and Science, later serving as a controller for the BBC.

Christopher Pinney is a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. His career includes appointments at the Australian National University, Northwestern University, and University College London, where he served as professor of anthropology and visual culture around 2000.

Christopher S. George works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Columbia University under Royal W. Weiler and Geshe Wangyal, founded the American Institute of Buddhist Studies, and held a professorship at the Institute for Advanced Studies of World Religions.

Christopher S. Queen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. His career includes positions at Harvard University as Dean of Students for Continuing Education and lecturer on religion and Buddhism.

Christopher V. Jones is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held appointments at the University of Oxford and the University of Cambridge, became an assistant professor at the University of Vienna in 2023, and joined the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Christopher Wallis specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Rochester, University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson, and University of California, Berkeley under Robert P. Goldman and Alexander von Rospatt, later serving as guest lecturer at Naropa University.

Christophorus Becker was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He founded the Missionsärztliches Institut Würzburg in 1923, taught there, and served as Privatdozent for mission studies at the University of Würzburg.

Chu-tsing Li was a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Nanking and University of Iowa, later serving as an art history professor at Iowa and on the faculty at the University of Kansas.
Chuichi Kimura is a scholar in Buddhist studies who held an associate professorship and professorship at Minobusan University.

Chulthim Gurung works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at the Karmapa International Buddhist Institute, University of British Columbia, and McGill University, he has served in administrative and teaching positions at these institutions and with the Karmapa International Buddhist Society.

Chun-i Tang was a philosopher and sinologist who studied at National Central University and Peking University under mentors including Shili Xiong. He was a professor at National Central University and founding chairman and Chair Professor at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
Chun-min Yen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who completed a PhD at the University of Arizona under Robert M. Gimello.
Chung-pui Tai is a scholar of linguistics, sinology, and Tibetology who studied at the Graduate School of Chinese Academy of Social Sciences and held a post at the University of Hong Kong.

Chögyam Trungpa was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Oxford University and under teachers including Khenpo Gangshar and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and he founded Naropa University and Kagyu Samye Ling.
Chökyi Gyatso studied under teachers such as Khakyab Dorje, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and both studied under and taught Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.
Chökyi Nyima studied under Dudjom Rinpoche and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

Chökyi Nyima Rinpoche works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He studied at Rumtek Monastery under the 16th Karmapa and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, served as abbot of Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling, and founded the Rangjung Yeshe Institute.
Chökyi Nyinche studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Shechen Gyaltsab, and taught Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche.
Chönyi Drolma is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Thinley Norbu Rinpoche, Lama Tharchin Rinpoche, and Ngawang Zangpo.
